column1: # Level-1 scripted route replay (issue #8). A `warp` per leg (except the level's own start), then a
# held-forward `input`.
# The warp poses are retail's own recorded route placements: the `walkplayer` things the level
# ships, read by retail's `coords` and committed in `tools/parity/shots.tsv` (the `route_*` rows)
# and `tools/parity/walk-shots.tsv` (the walk legs). They are camera EYES in world units; the
# replay puts the body one template eye offset below (the same subtraction retail's `warp` and
# this port's `--warp` do), so both sides' bodies start at the same point.
# `input <ticks> <forward> <strafe>` holds that intent for the ticks; the capture step is 1/60 s.
# A leg's length is its retail trace's held-key window (600 ms per retail sample), so the port's
# 600 ms samples fall on the same ticks as the retail capture's `held_ms` samples.
#   leg      ticks  retail source
#   spawn     180   tools/parity/walktrace/spawn-walk.tsv  (5 x 600 ms; retaken from retail's
#                   recorded spawn pose; the level's own start is the same pose)
#   cantina   144   tools/parity/walktrace/walk_cantina-walk.tsv (4 x 600 ms)
#   street    180   tools/parity/walktrace/walk_street45-walk.tsv (5 x 600 ms)
#   door      180   tools/parity/walktrace/walk_door0-walk.tsv (5 x 600 ms)
# The three committed legs are the same rows `trace-gate.ps1` replays; the spawn leg is the level's
# own start pose. A leg boundary is a `warp`, not a walk: the retail reference is four separate
# per-leg captures from the level's own authored placements, so the route is the same four walks.
# Issue #10 fixed what each leg exposed — the spawn seat, the engine's walk rate, and the attach
# height a `warp` leaves a body at — so the legs now hold retail's sectors and vertical travel.
# Scenario rows (no tick cost, so the sample grid stays on retail's 600 ms cadence):
#   seed <vx> <vy>   start a leg at the velocity the retail capture already had at its pose (its
#                    first 600 ms already covered the leg's travel; the fixture's row-0 `vel` is 0
#                    only because that window has no earlier sample).
# There is no `switch` row: retail's own `cogstatus 11` reads `doorstatus 0` after the cantina walk
# with that door already open, and the replay's synthetic `activate` (the only thing that made the
# port read 2) is a scenario the retail capture never performed. Without it the replay's positions
# are unchanged and its switch cog reads retail's value; the gate compares the two now.
# The street leg holds 90°, the direction retail's body actually travelled: the capture's 45° input
# was clamped by the doorway jamb, and the port's door leaf sits 0.035 units from retail's, so the
# recorded path is replayed rather than the clamp offset.
# The spawn leg carries no pose: retail's spawn trace starts at the level's own start (it is not a
# `warp` capture), and the engine does not attach a body that was placed at load — it falls from the
# authored pose to the swept sphere contact (z -1.13 -> -1.18). A warp here would attach it at model
# height and hold z where retail shows it falling.
# kind
warp
seed
input
warp
input
warp
input
warp
input
# Exit segment (issue #15): door0 opened by the player's own use key, **walked through**, then the
# level's own upper-route placements and the one-way door to the 8t88 landing.
# The `door` leg above ends at tick 684 on the retail walk's own stop pose (1.30, 9.07, sector 328),
# which is what the frozen retail fixture's last row records. The exit segment does not walk on from
# there: `00_door.cog`'s `startup` hid the door sector's adjoins, so the walk stops at the portal with
# the linked leaf 0.5 beyond it — outside the 0.165 use sweep. It warps instead to the port's stop pose,
# derived from the level geometry: eye (1.28, 9.62, 6.357114), sector 60, yaw 105, where the eye is 0.086
# from the linked leaf (thing 4 at 1.200002, 9.650073, 6.35) at a 0.81 facing dot. It is **not**
# placement 174's eye: committed `walkplayer` placement 174 is (1.400084, 9.700065, 6.357114), 0.206 from
# the leaf and outside the reach, and there is no walktrace of the exit door. `use` presses the player's
# ACTIVATE binding (scancode 0x39, SPACE: the profile's `bind 12 57 0x2`; the PLR stores scancodes, so
# the earlier `9` sent the wrong key), which `sithPlayerActions_Activate` (`0x4fc0a0`) answers by
# `activated` (id 1); `00_door.cog` reopens the adjoins and runs `OpenDoors`. `wait 72` lets the leaf
# reach frame 1; `yaw 0` turns the body to the doorway (the door leg's own heading) and `input 108`
# walks it through the opening — the trace's y passes the leaf's 9.650073 on that hold, which is the
# crossing the retail fixture has no rows for. Sector 60 spans both sides of the leaf, so the sector
# column does not change.
# `exit_upper` is placement 175 (-2.519, 11.001, 6.72 body), `exit_low` placement 176
# (-6.15, 9.65, 4.32 body), and `exit_tunnel` is the sector-407 tunnel mouth in front of the one-way
# door (thing 47 at -4.05, 13.95, 4.375; `00_1waydoor.cog` opens it for a body inside 407). The tunnel
# hold crosses 407 -> 223 -> 229 -> 215 and the renderer sights 8t88 on the way: `sithRender_RenderThing`
# (`0x4c8070`) sends `sighted` to `01_goal0.cog`, which reports the objective, and `01_endlevel.cog`'s
# `user0` sets goal bin 100 = 3, sleeps 3 s and calls `jkEndLevel(1)`. The trailing `wait` outlasts that
# sleep, so the last sample carries `level_end` 1 — the level finished through its own scripts.
warp
use
wait
yaw
input
